 Oral Judgment
Though the appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 08.04.2024 passed by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi, in MVC No.611 of 2022.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The claimant met with an accident on 21.04.2022 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bolero Pick Up Van bearing registration No.MH-24/AU-1813 and sustained grievous injures.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6622 HC-KAR
Therefore, he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.21,12,800/-.

4. The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.5,08,900/-
with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the same with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

5. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, PW.2-Doctor has assessed the disability at 33%, but the Tribunal has Parameshwar vs Laxman And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64456908/
2 taken the disability at only 11%; though he was earning Rs.18,000/- per month, his income was taken only at Rs.14,750/- per month and meagre amount was granted towards medical bills and also under other heads.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6622 HC-KAR 7.

As the appellant was failed to prove his income, the Tribunal has taken his notional income at Rs.14,750/- per month as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, as the accident is of the year 2022 and it needs no interference.
The appellant sustained fracture of right tibia and fibula.

He examined the Doctor as PW.2 and as per X-ray report-Ex.P9, he found that,
there is evidence of old fracture of middle third shaft of right tibia with internal fixation of rod and screws seen in situ and fracture of middle third shaft of right fibula and assessed the disability at 33% to the whole body.
The Tribunal has taken 1/3rd of the same as 11% and this Court finds no reason to interfere with the same.

Further, as the appellant was aged 25 years, the Tribunal has applied the multiplier of '18' and has awarded an amount of Rs.3,50,500/- (Rs.14,750 x 12 x 18 x 11%
= Rs.3,50,460, rounded off to Rs.3,50,500) towards loss of future earnings, which is just and proper and needs no interference.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6622 HC-KAR 8.
The Tribunal has also granted Rs.73,400/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.
9. The appellant was doing private work and he was admitted in the hospital for 10 days.

Considering his age, occupation, nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.50,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.40,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
10. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of six months due to the injuries sustained.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.88,500/-
(Rs.14,750 x 6) for loss of income during laid up period.
11. The Tribunal has also granted an amount of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses and it needs no interference.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6622 HC-KAR 12.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.73,400/-
Future medical expenses Rs.20,000/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.3,50,500/-
Parameshwar vs Laxman And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64456908/

3 Loss of income during laid up period Rs.88,500/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.40,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-
Total Rs.7,22,400/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.5,08,900/-
Enhancement Rs.2,13,500/-
The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,13,500/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

13. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.2,13,500/- with interest at NC: 2025:KHC-K:6622 HC-KAR 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) As there was no driving licence to the driver of the offending vehicle, the Tribunal has ordered for pay and recovery.
Therefore, respondent No.2-Insurance Company is at liberty to recover the above amount from respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle by due process of law.
(v) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
